$comment: Design-system PROJECT REGISTRY. One entry per Figma-backed design system this repo drives. Read by libs/altitude-mcp/src/lib/ds-project.mjs, which resolves the active project from --project <id>, the DS_PROJECT env var, or `default` below. Everything that used to be a hardcoded 'Altitude' string in the parity tooling (Figma file key, manifest path, prompt pipeline, Storybook identity) now comes from here.

decoys.why: Empty scratch file; an earlier pass built 31 component sets into it by mistake. Refuse to write here.

library.//excludeTitlePrefixes: SCOPE, not presentation. Story titles under these prefixes are not COMPONENTS of this design system, so parity must not report them as missing in Figma. This used to live under `storybook`, which was wrong twice over: it is a library-scope concern, and it made the field disappear when Southleft's Storybook was retired on 2026-08-23.

excluded.al-theme-switcher: Owns no pixels — an al-button + al-popover + al-menu composition; a Figma set would duplicate three components (altitude-figma-sync: NOT_COMPONENTS).
excluded.al-icon: Icons live in Figma as 71 flat components on the 🛠 Icons page (resolved by name), not as a component set — there is nothing for a per-set parity check to bind to.

southleft.name: Southleft Design System

library.$componentsComment: SCOPE. Southleft's design system is the subset of @southleft/al-web-components that southleft.com actually ships, not the whole 105-component Altitude catalog. Derived from `grep -rhoE '<al-[a-z0-9-]+' apps/southleft/src --include=*.astro` and re-checkable with scripts/check-sl-scope.mjs. Adding a component to the SITE is what earns it a place here; keep the two in step or the DS documents things Southleft does not use and the parity list fills with noise.
library.//excludeTitlePrefixes: SCOPE, not presentation. Story titles under these prefixes are not COMPONENTS of this design system, so parity must not report them as missing in Figma. This used to live under `storybook`, which was wrong twice over: it is a library-scope concern, and it made the field disappear when Southleft's Storybook was retired on 2026-08-23.

southleft.$brandLibraryComment: THE SECOND LAYER. `library` above is SHARED — Altitude documents all of @southleft/al-web-components and Southleft documents 21 of it — so nothing brand-specific can live there. The page sections that ARE Southleft (hero, cta band, marquee, media card, logo wall, section header, page hero, and the brand header/footer) are a separate package, @southleft/sl-web-components, built on top of Altitude. They had their own Storybook until it was retired on 2026-08-23, which is when they stopped being documented anywhere: apps/docs read one manifest. Declaring the layer here is what puts them back on /docs/southleft, and it is generic — any project may declare one.

brandLibrary.$supersedesComment: SAME TAG, BRAND IMPLEMENTATION. A brand layer publishes al-* tags like everything else â one namespace, so a page is authored in al-* and never mixes two (spec 2026-08-23-one-al-namespace-across-brand-and-base). Where a brand component MODIFIES a base one they share the tag outright: `al-header` and `al-footer` here are Southleft's, and the app imports this package's module instead of the base one, so exactly one definition exists at runtime. `supersedes` maps the tag to itself to say that this is deliberate override rather than an accidental collision â the docs site documents the brand implementation under that tag and drops the base record for this project.

excluded.al-theme-switcher: Owns no pixels — an al-button + al-popover + al-menu composition; a Figma set would duplicate three components.
excluded.al-icon: Icons are a 1,512-glyph Phosphor catalog resolved by name, not a component set — nothing for a per-set parity check to bind to.
excluded.al-theme: The theming HOST — sets brand/mode/density tokens on :host and owns no pixels of its own. Nothing for Figma to mirror.

docs.//: Southleft's Storybook was retired (2026-08-23). The multi-brand docs site at apps/docs serves this project at /docs/southleft/, generated from the same CEM, so a second Storybook was duplicating it. `route` is what apps/docs already derives for a non-default project; `productionBase` is where that lands when deployed.
